title: packages API: `POST /api/v1/packages?overwrite=true` replaces a read-only package's registry row (201), where disable, publish, revert and delete refuse it `WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED`
body:
Filing gate: one class (a) out-of-scope finding from the #23972 round-2 dev report `6223094149`. Its reach was measured at the public door. Filed by `domain:spec` seat 2 (seat post #18549) · `os-bill` · session `session_01LFqdRsuM5nkqoJdHd5ztVk`, as the seat that dispatched #23972. ⛔ Not a claim; the grade and the lane are triage's.

## Measured

The #23972 dev measured this at PR #24010's head `7c45b88c05`, with a throwaway probe on the runtime dispatcher test harness that was deleted afterwards:

- `POST /api/v1/packages?overwrite=true` with a manifest whose `id` `ObjectQL.registerApp` booted answers **201**. That holds on both limbs: the `protocol` service's `installPackage`, and the no-protocol fallback.
- The registry row is replaced: version `2.0.0` in the probe, and `source: 'authored'` once #23972 lands.
- `engine.manifests` still holds the id, so the served row reads `writable: false`. One row then says an org authored this package, while the server treats it as read-only.

## The code (`main` `bb14934cda`, `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts`)

- `:1373`–`:1380`: `overwrite` only bypasses the `409 Package '…' already exists`. Nothing asks whether the id is a read-only package.
- `:1396` (the protocol limb) and `:1409` (the fallback limb) write the registry row.
- The other lifecycle doors call `requireWritablePackage` (`:517`) first: disable `:1569`, publish `:1596`, revert `:2073`, delete `:2268`. On a package `isWritablePackage` judges read-only, each answers `422 WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED` with the sentence "it is read-only (provided by code or an installed app). Packages the deployment ships are managed by the deployment, not over this API".

So the same rule has two answers at one route family. Disable, delete, publish and revert refuse to touch a shipped package, but replacing it outright goes through.

`Governing text:` ADR-0070 D2, the read-only package rule that `isWritablePackage` implements (`docs/adr/0070-package-first-authoring.md`, the `docs` link the `WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED` refusal carries).

## Not measured

- Whether the protocol limb's persisted `sys_packages` row survives a restart alongside the code registration of the same id, and which of the two the registry holds after boot.
- Which callers hold the permission this door requires.

## What done looks like

- An overwrite whose id `isWritablePackage` judges read-only (booted by code, installed from the marketplace, or with a `system` / `cloud` scope) is refused with the `requireWritablePackage` answer. The refusal comes before any registry or `sys_packages` write, on both limbs.
- Pins:
  - an overwrite over a code-booted id is refused, and the registry row and `engine.manifests` are unchanged;
  - an overwrite over a marketplace-installed id is refused;
  - CONTROL: an overwrite over an authored base still answers 201.
- ⛔ The rule is not re-derived at this door: it reads `isWritablePackage`, as the four doors above do.

## Related

- #23974 (open) names the same `POST /api/v1/packages` door for a different gap: the ADR-0087 conversion. The two edit the same region of `packages.ts`, so whichever is dispatched second queues behind the other.
- #23972 (PR #24010, in review) stamps `source` at this door. It does not change the overwrite path.

Dedupe: MCP `search_issues` in objectstack-ai/objectstack, closed included, for `POST /packages overwrite replaces a read-only code package registry row booted by registerApp` and `install package overwrite read-only package writable_package_required authoring door`. Neither query returned a card about this path. The nearest are #23974 (the same door, the conversion gap) and #22689 (closed; registry `_packageVersion` on `registerItem`).
